blurb.en: Learn topic words, -ed and -ing words, comparing words and partners like good at.
blurb.vi: Học từ vựng chủ đề, từ đuôi -ed và -ing, từ so sánh và cặp từ như good at.

generous.def: Happy to give your time, money or things to other people.
generous.ex: My *generous* uncle shared his sweets with all the children.

outgoing.def: Friendly and happy to talk to new people.
outgoing.ex: Zara is very *outgoing*. She made five new friends on her first day.

bad-tempered.def: Often cross or angry, even about small things.
bad-tempered.ex: Our old cat gets *bad-tempered* when she is hungry.

enormous.ex: There is an *enormous* tree in the middle of the square.

mysterious.def: Strange, and hard to understand or explain.
mysterious.ex: We found a *mysterious* old key under the stairs.

fever.def: When your body is too hot because you are ill.
fever.ex: Kai stayed in bed because he had a *fever*.

sore throat.def: A pain inside your neck that makes it hurt to talk or swallow.
sore throat.ex: I have a *sore throat*, so Mum made me some warm honey water.

dairy products.def: Food made from milk, like cheese, yoghurt and butter.
dairy products.ex: *Dairy products* give us calcium for strong bones and teeth.

fibre.def: A part of vegetables, fruit and brown rice that helps your stomach work well.
fibre.ex: Beans and apples have lots of *fibre*.

sketch.def: A quick drawing with a pencil, often made before a painting.
sketch.ex: The artist made a *sketch* of the street before she painted it.

pattern.def: Shapes, lines or colours that repeat again and again.
pattern.ex: My scarf has a *pattern* of red and white stars.

fireworks.def: Things that explode in the night sky with bright colours and loud bangs.
fireworks.ex: At midnight we watched the *fireworks* over the river.

feast.def: A very big, special meal for a lot of people.
feast.ex: For the New Year, Grandma cooked a *feast* for twenty people.

chewy.def: Soft, but you need to bite it many times before you can swallow it.
chewy.ex: The rice cakes were sweet and *chewy*.

title.vi: Tính từ đuôi -ed / -ing và trật tự tính từ

scenes.head: A page from Theo's diary
scenes.html: On Saturday morning I was *bored*. The rain was *boring*, and I had nothing to do. Then Dad took me to see the street art in Chalk Lane. On one wall there was a *beautiful big blue* waterfall. It looked so real! I was *amazed*, and I touched it. It was only paint on a *tall old brick* wall! The artist showed us her pencil sketches. 'Tricks like this are *exciting*, aren't they?' she said. I was *excited* all the way home.

steps.en: Words with *-ed* tell us how a person feels: I was *bored*, I was *amazed*, I was *excited*.
steps.vi: Từ có đuôi *-ed* cho biết một người cảm thấy thế nào: I was *bored*, I was *amazed*, I was *excited*.

steps.en: Words with *-ing* tell us what makes us feel that way: the rain was *boring*, tricks are *exciting*.
steps.vi: Từ có đuôi *-ing* cho biết điều gì làm ta có cảm giác đó: the rain was *boring*, tricks are *exciting*.

steps.en: Two or three adjectives before a noun go in this order: opinion, size, age, colour, material.
steps.vi: Khi có hai hoặc ba tính từ đứng trước danh từ, ta xếp theo thứ tự: ý kiến, kích thước, tuổi, màu sắc, chất liệu.

steps.en: So we say a *beautiful big blue* waterfall and a *tall old brick* wall.
steps.vi: Vì vậy ta nói a *beautiful big blue* waterfall và a *tall old brick* wall.

title.vi: So sánh hơn và so sánh nhất

scenes.head: Ruby's food blog: New Year snacks
scenes.html: At New Year, Grandma made three snacks. First, I tried the sticky rice cake. It was boiled for ten hours, so it was *softer than* bread. Next, I ate the coconut sweets. They were *sweeter than* the rice cake, and very chewy. But *the chewiest* snack was the ginger sweets! My favourite was the rice cake. It was *the most delicious* snack on the table, and it was *better than* any cake from a shop!

steps.en: To compare two things, add *-er* and use *than*: *softer than*, *sweeter than*.
steps.vi: Để so sánh hai thứ, thêm *-er* và dùng *than*: *softer than*, *sweeter than*.

steps.en: For the top one in a group, use *the* + *-est*: *the chewiest* snack.
steps.vi: Để nói thứ đứng đầu trong một nhóm, dùng *the* + *-est*: *the chewiest* snack.

steps.en: Long adjectives use *more* and *the most*: *the most delicious*.
steps.vi: Tính từ dài dùng *more* và *the most*: *the most delicious*.
*Good* là tính từ đặc biệt: good, *better*, *the best*.

title.vi: Cặp từ (tính từ + giới từ) và đoán nghĩa từ mới

scenes.head: From our class magazine: Our caretaker
scenes.html: Everyone knows our school caretaker. He is *kind to* every child, and he is *good at* fixing things. Last week he mended our broken classroom door in ten minutes! He is *interested in* plants too, and he grows tomatoes behind the school hall. He is always cheerful. He smiles and sings, even on rainy days. When he was young, he was *afraid of* dogs, but now he looks after the school's old dog, Biscuit. We are all *proud of* him.

steps.en: Some adjectives always have the same little word after them: *kind to*, *good at*, *interested in*.
steps.vi: Một số tính từ luôn đi với cùng một giới từ phía sau: *kind to*, *good at*, *interested in*.

steps.en: Learn them as pairs: *afraid of*, *proud of*, *worried about*, *famous for*.
steps.vi: Hãy học chúng theo cặp: *afraid of*, *proud of*, *worried about*, *famous for*.

steps.en: Don't know cheerful? Read the next sentence: he smiles and sings, even on rainy days. So he is always happy!
steps.vi: Chưa biết từ cheerful? Hãy đọc câu tiếp theo: ông ấy cười và hát, kể cả vào ngày mưa. Vậy ông ấy luôn vui vẻ!

end.en: Great work! You found the special words in all three texts.
end.vi: Làm tốt lắm! Em đã tìm được các từ đặc biệt trong cả ba bài đọc.

challenge.result: You spotted -ed and -ing words, comparing words, word partners and adjective order.

v.q: The rain was boring, so Theo felt ________.
whys: Boring is for the thing (the rain). Theo is a person with a feeling.
Boredom is a noun. After 'felt' we need an adjective.
v.hint: Is the gap about a person's feeling or about the thing?
v.worked: Theo is a person and the gap is his feeling, so we use *-ed*: 'Theo felt *bored*.'

v.q: The painting looked so real. It was ________!
whys: Amazed is how a person feels. Here we talk about the painting.
Amaze is a verb. After 'It was' we need an adjective.
v.hint: Who or what is 'It'? A person or a thing?
v.worked: 'It' is the painting, a thing that makes us feel amazed, so we use *-ing*: 'It was *amazing*!'

v.q: Grandma's rice cake was ________ than bread.
whys: Softest is for the top one in a group. Look at 'than'.
Soft does not compare. Look at the word after the gap.
v.hint: Look at the word after the gap. What does 'than' tell you?
v.worked: We compare two things with *-er* + *than*: 'softer than bread'.

v.q: The ________ snack of all was the ginger sweets.
whys: Chewier compares only two things. Read 'of all'.
Chewy does not tell us it is the top one. Read 'of all'.
v.hint: Read the end of the sentence. Is it one of two, or the top one of all?
v.worked: 'The ... of all' tells us it is the top one, so we use *the chewiest*.

v.q: The caretaker is good ________ fixing things.
whys: We say 'interested in', but not 'good in' for a skill.
'Good for' means healthy for you, like 'Fruit is good for you'.
v.hint: Which little word goes with 'good' when you talk about a skill?
v.worked: The partner of good for a skill is *at*: 'good at fixing things'.

v.q: He is interested ________ plants and grows tomatoes.
whys: 'Interested on' is not English. Check the partner of 'interested'.
'Interested at' is not English. 'At' goes with 'good'.
v.hint: Which little word always comes after 'interested'?
v.worked: The partner of interested is *in*: 'interested in plants'.

v.q: On one wall there was a ________ waterfall.
whys: Your opinion (beautiful) comes first, before size and colour.
Colour comes after opinion and size, not first.
v.hint: Remember the order: opinion, size, age, colour, material.
v.worked: Opinion, size, colour: a *beautiful big blue* waterfall.

v.q: It was only paint on a ________ wall!
whys: Material (brick) comes last, just before the noun.
Size (tall) comes before age (old).
v.hint: Remember the order: opinion, size, age, colour, material.
v.worked: Size, age, material: a *tall old brick* wall.

title.vi: Từ vựng chủ đề của Bài 1 đến Bài 4

v.q: Anya always shares her snacks and lends her pens to everyone. She is ________.
whys: A selfish person keeps things for himself or herself. Anya shares.
A bad-tempered person gets angry. The sentence is about sharing.
v.hint: What does Anya do with her snacks and pens?
v.worked: 'Always shares her snacks and lends her pens' tells us Anya is *generous*.

v.q: My little brother gets angry about small things and often shouts. He is ________.
whys: An outgoing person is friendly with new people. Is shouting friendly?
A generous person likes to give. The sentence is about getting angry.
v.hint: What does the brother do when small things happen?
v.worked: 'Gets angry about small things and often shouts' tells us he is *bad-tempered*.

v.q: I can't stop coughing, and it hurts when I swallow. What have I got?
whys: An earache is a pain in your ear. Where does it hurt when you swallow?
A runny nose is about your nose, not about swallowing.
v.hint: Where in your body do you feel it when you swallow?
v.worked: 'It hurts when I swallow' tells us the pain is in the throat: *a sore throat*.

v.q: Milk, cheese and yoghurt are all ...
whys: Grains are rice, bread and cereals. What are milk and cheese made from?
Vegetables grow in the ground. Milk and cheese don't grow.
v.hint: What do milk, cheese and yoghurt all come from?
v.worked: Milk, cheese and yoghurt are all made from milk, so they are *dairy products*.

v.q: Type the missing word. It starts with f.
lines: For the New Year, Grandma cooked a big {0} for all the family.
v.hint: Which word means a very big, special meal? It has 5 letters.
v.worked: A very big, special meal for lots of people is a *feast*.

v.q: Type the missing word. It starts with s.
lines: The artist drew a quick {0} with her pencil before she started to paint.
v.hint: Which word means a quick pencil drawing? It has 6 letters.
v.worked: A quick drawing with a pencil before a painting is a *sketch*.

title.vi: Tính từ: cảm xúc, trật tự và so sánh

v.q: The film about the deep ocean was really ________. I want to see it again!
whys: Interested is how a person feels. Here we talk about the film.
Interest is a noun or a verb. After 'was really' we need an adjective.
v.hint: Is the gap about the film or about a person's feeling?
v.worked: The film makes us feel interested, so the film is *interesting* (-ing for the thing).

v.q: Jade had nothing to do at home all day, so she felt ________.
whys: Boring is for a thing or an activity. Jade is a person.
Boredom is a noun. After 'felt' we need an adjective.
v.hint: Jade is a person. Do we need -ed or -ing for a person's feeling?
v.worked: Jade is a person describing her feeling, so we use *-ed*: 'she felt *bored*'.

v.q: Choose the right order. Grandpa wears a ________ hat.
whys: Colour (brown) comes after opinion and age.
Your opinion (lovely) comes first, not last.
v.hint: Remember: opinion, size, age, colour, material.
v.worked: Opinion, age, colour: a *lovely old brown* hat.

v.q: Choose the right order. We live in a ________ flat near the park.
whys: Colour (white) comes after size and age.
Size (small) comes before age (new).
v.hint: Remember: opinion, size, age, colour, material.
v.worked: Size, age, colour: a *small new white* flat.

v.q: Type the right form of the word in brackets.
lines: An elephant is {0} (big) than a horse.
v.hint: Look at 'than'. For short words like big, double the last letter before you add the ending.
v.worked: Two things with *than*: big becomes *bigger*: 'bigger than a horse'.

v.q: Type the right form of the word in brackets.
lines: Today is the {0} (hot) day of the year!
v.hint: Look at 'the' and 'of the year'. For short words like hot, double the last letter.
v.worked: The top one of a group: hot becomes *the hottest*: 'the hottest day of the year'.

title.vi: Cặp từ: tính từ + giới từ

v.q: Minh is afraid ________ big dogs, so he crosses the road when he sees one.
whys: 'Afraid at' is not English. Check the partner of 'afraid'.
'Afraid in' is not English. 'In' goes with 'interested'.
v.hint: Which little word always comes after 'afraid'?
v.worked: The partner of afraid is *of*: 'afraid of big dogs'.

v.q: Our town is famous ________ its old market and its noodle soup.
whys: We say 'proud of', but 'famous' has a different partner.
'Famous at' is not English. 'At' goes with 'good'.
v.hint: Which little word comes after 'famous' to give the reason?
v.worked: The partner of famous is *for*: 'famous for its old market'.

v.q: Type the missing little word.
lines: Kai is very good {0} drawing animals.
v.hint: Drawing is a skill. Which little word goes with 'good' for a skill?
v.worked: For a skill we say *good at*: 'good at drawing animals'.

v.q: Type the missing little word.
lines: Linh is worried {0} her maths test tomorrow.
v.hint: Which little word comes after 'worried'? It has 5 letters.
v.worked: The partner of worried is *about*: 'worried about her maths test'.

v.q: Our teacher was ________ of us because we all worked so hard.
whys: Kind goes with 'to': kind to someone. Check the word after the gap.
Good goes with 'at': good at something. Check the word after the gap.
v.hint: Look at the little word after the gap. Which adjective is its partner?
v.worked: 'Worked so hard' makes a teacher happy and *proud*: 'proud of us'.

v.q: Please be ________ to the new boy. It's his first day at our school.
whys: We say 'afraid of', not 'afraid to' a person.
We say 'interested in', not 'interested to' a person.
v.hint: Look at the little word after the gap. Which adjective is its partner?
v.worked: The partner of kind is *to*: 'be kind to the new boy'.

blurb.en: Like the real Reading paper: choose the word, complete a message and fill a letter from a word box.
blurb.vi: Giống bài thi Đọc thật: chọn từ, hoàn thành tin nhắn và điền từ trong khung vào lá thư.

v.q: Felix was very ________ when his teacher said the class was going to visit Stone Hill Castle.
whys: Exciting is for the thing that makes you feel excited, like the trip. Felix is a person.
Excitement is a noun. After 'was very' we need an adjective.
v.hint: The gap is about Felix. Is it his feeling, or a thing?
v.worked: Felix is a person and the gap is his feeling, so we use *-ed*: 'Felix was very *excited*'.

v.q: Anya practised her New Year dance for two hours every evening, so the week was very ________ for her.
whys: Tired is how a person feels. Here the gap is about the week.
Tiredness is a noun. After 'was very' we need an adjective.
v.hint: What is the gap about: Anya, or the week?
v.worked: The week made Anya feel tired, so the week was *tiring* (-ing for the thing).

v.q: The castle was much ________ than Felix expected, with forty rooms and five tall towers.
whys: Biggest is for the top one in a group. Look at 'than'.
Big does not compare. Look at 'much' and 'than'.
v.hint: Look at the word after the gap.
v.worked: 'Much ... than' compares two things, so we use *bigger*: 'much bigger than Felix expected'.

v.q: On the night of the show, Anya wore the ________ dress in the whole group, with gold and red stars.
whys: More beautiful compares two things. Read 'in the whole group'.
Beautiful does not say it is the top one. Read 'in the whole group'.
v.hint: Read the end of the sentence. Is it one of two, or the top one of a group?
v.worked: 'The ... in the whole group' needs a superlative: *the most beautiful* dress.

v.q: Inside the castle, Felix's friend Hugo was afraid ________ the dark rooms, so Felix held his hand.
whys: 'Afraid at' is not English. 'At' goes with 'good'.
We say 'worried about', but 'afraid' has a different partner.
v.hint: Which little word always comes after 'afraid'?
v.worked: The partner of afraid is *of*: 'afraid of the dark rooms'.

v.q: After the show, Anya's grandparents hugged her and said they were very proud ________ her.
whys: 'Proud for' is not the right partner. Check the word that goes with 'proud'.
'Proud at' is not English. 'At' goes with 'good'.
v.hint: Which little word always comes after 'proud'?
v.worked: The partner of proud is *of*: 'proud of her'.

title.vi: Đọc Phần 2: hoàn thành tin nhắn

v.q: Which option correctly completes the message?
whys: We say 'interested in', but 'good' has a different partner for a skill.
'Good for' means healthy for you. Building things is a skill.
v.hint: Building things is a skill. Which little word goes with 'good' for a skill?
v.worked: For a skill we say *good at*: 'You're really good at building things.'

'Worried at' is not English. Check the partner of 'worried'.

Excitement is a noun. After 'It was so' we need an adjective.

v.worked: The sign asks how a person feels, so we use *-ed*: 'Feeling *tired* in the hot sun?'

stim.head: Sign at the sports field

v.q: Which option correctly completes the notice?
whys: Size (small) comes before colour, not at the end.
Material (plastic) comes last, just before the noun.
v.hint: Remember: opinion, size, age, colour, material.
v.worked: Size, colour, material: a *small blue plastic* pencil case.

v.q: Which option correctly completes the message?
whys: Best is for the top one in a group. Look at 'than'.
Good does not compare. Look at 'than last year'.
v.hint: Look at the word after the gap.
v.worked: 'Than last year' compares two years, and good becomes *better*: 'better than last year'.

lines: Now it is much bigger {0} the old library.

items.en: Use *-ed* for how a person feels. Use *-ing* for the thing that makes you feel it.
items.vi: Dùng đuôi *-ed* để nói một người cảm thấy thế nào. Dùng đuôi *-ing* cho sự vật làm ta có cảm giác đó.
example: I was *bored* because the film was *boring*.
The trip was *exciting*. We were all *excited*.

items.en: Before a noun, put adjectives in this order: opinion, size, age, colour, material.
items.vi: Trước danh từ, xếp tính từ theo thứ tự: ý kiến, kích thước, tuổi, màu sắc, chất liệu.

items.en: To compare two things, use *-er + than* for short words and *more ... than* for long words.
items.vi: Để so sánh hai thứ, dùng *-er + than* với từ ngắn và *more ... than* với từ dài.
example: A cheetah is *faster than* a horse.
Science is *more interesting than* I thought.

items.en: For the top one in a group, use *the -est* or *the most*. Good, better, best and bad, worse, worst are special.
items.vi: Để nói thứ đứng đầu trong một nhóm, dùng *the -est* hoặc *the most*. Good, better, best và bad, worse, worst là dạng đặc biệt.
example: It was *the hottest* day of the year.

items.en: Some adjectives have a partner word: *good at*, *interested in*, *afraid of*, *proud of*, *kind to*, *worried about*, *famous for*.
items.vi: Một số tính từ có giới từ đi kèm: *good at*, *interested in*, *afraid of*, *proud of*, *kind to*, *worried about*, *famous for*.
example: I'm *worried about* my cat. She's ill.

items.en: Don't know a word? Read the sentences *before* and *after* it. Look for an example or an explanation.
items.vi: Không biết một từ? Hãy đọc câu *trước* và *sau* nó. Tìm ví dụ hoặc lời giải thích.
example: Our neighbour is very talkative. *She chats to everyone for hours.*
The cave was gloomy. *It was dark and a bit scary.*

check.sentence: I felt {bored|boring|boredom} in the long queue at the bank.
My grandpa has a {lovely old brown|brown old lovely|old lovely brown} hat.
A train is {faster|fastest|fast} than a bike.
This is the {most beautiful|more beautiful|beautiful} park in our city.
Zara is very good {at|in|on} drawing horses.
Kai is talkative: he chats all day. Talkative means {he talks a lot|he is very quiet|he is often late}.

v.q: Theo's big sister is really good ________ maths, so she helps him with his homework every evening.
whys: We say 'interested in', but 'good' has a different partner for a skill.
'Good on' is not the right partner. Check the word that goes with 'good'.
v.hint: Maths is a skill here. Which little word goes with 'good'?
v.worked: For a skill we say *good at*: 'really good at maths'.

v.q: Zara is interested ________ animals, and she wants to be a vet when she grows up.
whys: 'At' goes with 'good', not with 'interested'.
'Interested for' is not English. Check the partner of 'interested'.
v.hint: Which little word always comes after 'interested'?
v.worked: The partner of interested is *in*: 'interested in animals'.

v.q: My grandma is very kind ________ everyone in our street, and she often cooks soup for her neighbours.
whys: 'Kind at' is not English. 'At' goes with 'good'.
'Kind in' is not English. 'In' goes with 'interested'.
v.hint: Which little word comes after 'kind' when we talk about other people?
v.worked: We are kind *to* people: 'kind to everyone in our street'.

v.q: Hugo was worried ________ his little sister because she had a high fever all night.
whys: 'Worried at' is not English. 'At' goes with 'good'.
'Worried in' is not English. Check the partner of 'worried'.
v.hint: Which little word always comes after 'worried'?
v.worked: The partner of worried is *about*: 'worried about his little sister'.

v.q: Brown rice has lots of fibre, so it is ________ for you than white rice.
whys: Best is for the top one in a group. Look at 'than'.
Good does not compare two things. Look at 'than'.
v.hint: Find 'than' in the sentence. What does it tell you?
v.worked: 'Than white rice' compares two foods, and good becomes *better*.

v.q: The new shopping centre in our town is ________ than the old market, but it is not as friendly.
whys: Biggest is for the top one in a group. Look at 'than'.
Big does not compare two places. Look at 'than'.
v.hint: Find 'than' in the sentence. What does it tell you?
v.worked: 'Than the old market' compares two places, so we use *bigger*.

v.q: The ________ building in our city is the new hotel. It has fifty floors!
whys: Taller compares two things, but there is no 'than' here.
Tall does not tell us it is the top one 'in our city'.
v.hint: Look at 'The' and 'in our city'. Is it the top one of a group?
v.worked: 'The ... in our city' tells us it is the top one: *the tallest* building.

v.q: Of all the dishes at the New Year feast, the sticky rice was the ________ popular with the children.
whys: More compares two things. Read 'Of all the dishes'.
Much does not make a superlative. Read 'Of all the dishes'.
v.hint: Read the start of the sentence: 'Of all the dishes'.
v.worked: 'Of all the dishes' means the top one, and popular is a long word: *the most popular*.

v.q: Kai stayed at home because he had ________ and felt very hot all night.
whys: A feast is a big special meal, not an illness.
Fibre is part of healthy food, not an illness.
v.hint: Kai felt very hot and stayed at home. What is wrong with him?
v.worked: Feeling very hot when you are ill means you have *a high fever*.

v.q: At midnight, everyone looked up at ________ in the night sky. Bang! Bang!
whys: Presents are gifts we give. They are not in the sky.
A feast is a big meal. It is not in the sky.
v.hint: What makes colours and loud bangs in the night sky?
v.worked: Colours and 'Bang! Bang!' in the night sky are *fireworks*.

v.q: Ruby thought the museum would be ________, but she loved the old maps and stayed for three hours.
whys: Bored is how a person feels. Here we talk about the museum.
Boredom is a noun. After 'would be' we need an adjective.
v.hint: What is the gap about: Ruby or the museum?
v.worked: The museum is a thing that can make you feel bored, so we use *-ing*: 'the museum would be *boring*'.

v.q: Minh was ________ when he saw that his grandparents had come all the way from Hue for his birthday.
whys: Surprising is for the thing or the news. Minh is a person with a feeling.
Surprise is a noun or a verb. After 'was' we need an adjective here.
v.hint: Who is the sentence about? Is the gap his feeling?
v.worked: Minh is a person and the gap is his feeling, so we use *-ed*: 'Minh was *surprised*'.

v.q: Which option correctly completes the notice?
whys: Colour (black) comes after size and age.
Size (big) comes before age (old).
v.hint: Remember: opinion, size, age, colour, material.
v.worked: Size, age, colour: a *big old black* umbrella.

stim.head: School notice
stim.html: FOUND near the school gate on Monday morning: a ________ umbrella with a white handle. Is it yours? Please ask at the school office. It will stay there until Friday.

v.q: Which option correctly completes the email?
whys: More interesting compares two places. Read 'of all'.
Interesting does not say it is the top one. Read 'of all'.
v.hint: Read the end of the sentence. Is it one of two, or the top one of all?
v.worked: 'The ... place of all' needs a superlative: *the most interesting* place.

stim.head: Email
stim.html:
Hi Jade,
Thanks for showing me around your town! Sun Lane, with all its street art, was the ________ place of all. I took fifty photos there!
See you soon,
Zara

v.q: Read Jade's email. Choose a word from the box for gap (1).
lines: I was worried {0} missing our class trip to the farm.
v.hint: Which word from the box is the partner of 'worried'?
v.worked: The partner of worried is *about*: 'worried about missing our class trip'.

stim.head: Email from Jade to her friend Kai
stim.html:
Word box: about, at, in, than, to, was

Hi Kai,
Sorry I wasn't at school last week. I (0) was ill with a fever and a sore throat. The doctor told me to rest and drink lots of water. I was worried (1) ________ missing our class trip to the farm, but Mum says the trip is next month now. Today I feel much better (2) ________ I did on Saturday, and I can eat properly again. Grandma brought me a bowl of chicken soup and a bunch of grapes. Everyone was so kind (3) ________ me! I'm coming back to school on Monday.
See you soon,
Jade

v.q: Read Anya's email. Choose a word from the box for gap (1).
lines: The girl is very good {0} climbing.
v.hint: Climbing is a skill. Which word from the box goes with 'good'?
v.worked: For a skill we say *good at*: 'very good at climbing'.

stim.head: Email from Anya to her friend Theo
stim.html:
Word box: at, for, is, most, of, than

Hi Theo,
I've just finished a brilliant book! It (0) is about a girl who finds an old map in her grandpa's box. The map shows a lost city in an enormous, mysterious jungle. The girl is very good (1) ________ climbing, so she climbs the tallest trees to look for the city. That is the (2) ________ exciting part of the book! At the end, she finds the city. It is famous (3) ________ its golden gates, but nobody has seen them for a hundred years. You can borrow the book next week.
Your friend,
Anya

v.q: Read Jade's email. Choose a word from the box for gap (2).
lines: Today I feel much better {0} I did on Saturday.
v.hint: Look at 'better'. She is comparing two days.
v.worked: She compares today and Saturday: 'much better *than* I did on Saturday'.

lines: That is the {0} exciting part of the book!
v.hint: Look at 'the'. Exciting is a long word. How do we make the top one?
v.worked: It is the top part of the whole book: 'the *most* exciting part'.

v.hint: Which word from the box comes after 'kind' when we talk about people?

goals: say how people feel and what things are like (bored / boring, excited / exciting)
put adjectives in the right order and compare things (bigger than, the most beautiful, the best)
use word partners like good at, afraid of, proud of and worried about
use topic words from all four units and guess a new word from the sentences around it
